We estimate the curvature term using the curvature norm. Recall that the curvature norm for KK along the HuH_{u} is weighted with f⁡(u)f(u). Using the Sobolev embedding theorem in Proposition 7, we have

‖∑i1+i2+i3≤3∇i1ψi2​∇i3K‖Lu¯1​L2​(S)≤C​f​(u)−1​(∑i1≤1,i2≤3‖∇i1ψ‖Lu¯2​L∞​(S)i2)​(∑i3≤3‖f⁡(u)​∇i3K‖Lu¯2​L2​(S))+C​f​(u)−1​‖∇2ψ‖Lu¯2​L4​(S)||f⁡(u)​K||Lu¯2​L4​(S)≤C​ϵ12​f​(u)−1​(∑i1≤3,i2≤3‖∇i1ψ‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S)i2)​(∑i3≤3‖f⁡(u)​∇i3K‖Lu¯2​L2​(S))≤C​ϵ12​f​(u)−1​(1+Δ1)3​ℛ.\begin{split}&||\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}\leq 3}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}K||_{L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\\ \leq&Cf(u)^{-1}(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 1,i_{2}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||^{i_{2}}_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)})(\sum_{i_{3}\leq 3}||f(u)\nabla^{i_{3}}K||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ &+Cf(u)^{-1}||\nabla^{2}\psi||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{4}(S)}||f(u)K||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{4}(S)}\\ \leq&C{\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}}f(u)^{-1}(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 3,i_{2}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||^{i_{2}}_{L^{{\infty}}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})(\sum_{i_{3}\leq 3}||f(u)\nabla^{i_{3}}K||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ \leq&C\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}f(u)^{-1}(1+\Delta_{1})^{3}\mathcal{R}.\end{split} (43)

The term linear in ∇4η\nabla^{4}\eta can be estimated analogously but using the 𝒪~4,2\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{4,2} norms instead of the ℛ\mathcal{R} norms:

‖∑i1+i2+i3≤3∇i1ψi2​∇i3+1η‖Lu¯1​L2​(S)≤C​ϵ​(∑i1≤3∑i2≤4‖∇i1ψ‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S)i2)+C​ϵ12​f​(u)−1​‖f⁡(u)​∇4η‖Lu¯2​L2​(S)≤C​ϵ​(1+Δ1)4+C​ϵ12​f​(u)−1​𝒪~4,2.\begin{split}&||\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}\leq 3}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}+1}\eta||_{L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\\ \leq&C\epsilon(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 3}\sum_{i_{2}\leq 4}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||^{i_{2}}_{L^{{\infty}}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})+C\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}f(u)^{-1}||f(u)\nabla^{4}\eta||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\\ \leq&C\epsilon(1+\Delta_{1})^{4}+C\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}f(u)^{-1}\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{4,2}.\end{split} (44)

We now move to control the terms that are nonlinear in the Ricci coefficients. First, we estimate the terms without ψH\psi_{H} or ψH¯\psi_{\underline{H}}:

‖∑i1+i2+i3+i4≤3∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψ​∇i4ψ‖Lu¯1​L2​(S)≤C​ϵ​(∑i1≤1,i2≤4‖∇i1ψ‖Lu¯∞​L∞​(S)i2)​(∑i3≤3‖∇i3ψ‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S))≤C​ϵ​(1+Δ1)5.\begin{split}&||\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}\leq 3}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi||_{L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\\ \leq&C\epsilon(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 1,i_{2}\leq 4}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}^{i_{2}})(\sum_{i_{3}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ \leq&C\epsilon(1+\Delta_{1})^{5}.\end{split} (45)

We then control the term with both ψH\psi_{H} and ψH¯\psi_{\underline{H}}:

‖∑i1+i2+i3+i4≤3∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψH​∇i4ψH¯‖Lu¯1​L2​(S)≤C⁡(∑i1≤1,i2≤3‖∇i1ψ‖Lu¯∞​L∞​(S)i2)​(∑i3≤1‖∇i3ψH¯‖Lu¯∞​L∞​(S))​(∑i4≤3‖∇i4ψH‖Lu¯1​L2​(S))+C⁡(∑i1≤1,i2≤3‖∇i1ψ‖Lu¯∞​L∞​(S)i2)​(∑i3≤3‖∇i3ψH¯‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S))​(∑i4≤1‖∇i4ψH‖Lu¯1​L∞​(S))+C​‖∇2ψ‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S)​‖ψH¯‖Lu¯∞​L∞​(S)||ψH||Lu¯1​L∞​(S)≤C⁡(∑i1≤1,i2≤3‖∇i1ψ‖Lu¯∞​L∞​(S)i2)​(∑i3≤1‖∇i3ψH¯‖Lu¯∞​L∞​(S))​(∑i4≤3‖f⁡(u¯)​∇i4ψH‖Lu¯2​L2​(S))||f​(u¯)−1||Lu¯2+C⁡(∑i1≤1,i2≤3‖∇i1ψ‖Lu¯∞​L∞​(S)i2)​(∑i3≤3‖∇i3ψH¯‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S))​(∑i4≤1‖f⁡(u¯)​∇i4ψH‖Lu¯2​L∞​(S))||f​(u¯)−1||Lu¯2+C​‖∇2ψ‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S)​‖ψH¯‖Lu¯∞​L∞​(S)​‖f⁡(u¯)​ψH‖Lu¯2​L∞​(S)||f​(u¯)−1||Lu¯2≤C​ϵ​(1+Δ1)3​(∑i1≤3‖f⁡(u¯)​∇i1ψH‖Lu¯2​L2​(S))​(∑i2≤3‖∇i2ψH¯‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S))≤C​ϵ​Δ1​(1+Δ1)3​(∑i≤3‖∇iψH¯‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S)).\begin{split}&||\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}\leq 3}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\\ \leq&C(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 1,i_{2}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}^{i_{2}})(\sum_{i_{3}\leq 1}||\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}{)}(\sum_{i_{4}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ &+C(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 1,i_{2}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}^{i_{2}})(\sum_{i_{3}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}{)}(\sum_{i_{4}\leq 1}||\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)})\\ &+C||\nabla^{2}\psi||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}||\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}||\psi_{H}||_{L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}\\ \leq&C(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 1,i_{2}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}^{i_{2}})(\sum_{i_{3}\leq 1}||\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}{)}(\sum_{i_{4}\leq 3}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})||f(\underline{u})^{-1}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}}\\ &+C(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 1,i_{2}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}^{i_{2}})(\sum_{i_{3}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}{)}(\sum_{i_{4}\leq 1}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)})||f(\underline{u})^{-1}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}}\\ &+C||\nabla^{2}\psi||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}||\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}||f(\underline{u})\psi_{H}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}||f(\underline{u})^{-1}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}}\\ \leq&C\epsilon(1+\Delta_{1})^{3}(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 3}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})(\sum_{i_{2}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{2}}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ \leq&C\epsilon\Delta_{1}(1+\Delta_{1})^{3}(\sum_{i\leq 3}||\nabla^{i}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}).\end{split} (46)

Therefore, by the bounds (43), (44), (45) and (46), we have that for every fixed uu,

∑i≤3‖∇iψH¯‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S)≤C⁡(∑i≤3‖∇iψH¯‖L2​(Su,0))+C​ϵ12​f​(u)−1​(ℛ+𝒪~4,2)+C​ϵ​(1+Δ1)5+C​ϵ​Δ1​(1+Δ1)3​(∑i≤3‖∇iψH¯‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S)).\begin{split}\sum_{i\leq 3}||\nabla^{i}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{{2}}(S)}\leq&{C(\sum_{i\leq 3}||\nabla^{i}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{2}(S_{u,0})})}+C\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}f(u)^{-1}(\mathcal{R}+\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{4,2})+C\epsilon(1+\Delta_{1})^{5}\\ &+C\epsilon\Delta_{1}(1+\Delta_{1})^{3}(\sum_{i\leq 3}||\nabla^{i}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}).\end{split}

We now multiply this inequality by f⁡(u)f(u) and take the L2L^{2} norm in uu to get

∑i≤3‖f⁡(u)​∇iψH¯‖Lu2​Lu¯∞​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)+C​ϵ12​‖f⁡(u)​(f​(u)−1)‖Lu2​(ℛ+𝒪~4,2)+C​ϵ​(1+Δ1)5+C​ϵ​Δ1​(1+Δ1)3​(∑i≤3‖f⁡(u)​∇iψH¯‖Lu2​Lu¯∞​L2​(S))≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i),\begin{split}&\sum_{i\leq 3}||f(u)\nabla^{i}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{2}_{u}L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\\ \leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})+C\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}||f(u)(f(u)^{-1})||_{L^{2}_{u}}(\mathcal{R}+\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{4,2})+C\epsilon(1+\Delta_{1})^{5}\\ &+C\epsilon\Delta_{1}(1+\Delta_{1})^{3}(\sum_{i\leq 3}||f(u)\nabla^{i}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{2}_{u}L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ \leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini}),\end{split}

for ϵ\epsilon sufficiently small. ∎

Using instead the equation for ∇3ψH\nabla_{3}\psi_{H}, we obtain the following estimates in a completely analogous manner:

Proposition 14.

Assume

ℛ<∞,𝒪~4,2<∞.\mathcal{R}<\infty,\quad\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{4,2}<\infty.

Then there exists ϵ0=ϵ0​(Δ1,ℛ,𝒪~4,2)\epsilon_{0}=\epsilon_{0}(\Delta_{1},\mathcal{R},\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{4,2}) such that whenever ϵ≤ϵ0\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{0},

∑i≤3𝒪i,2​[ψH]≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i).\sum_{i\leq 3}\mathcal{O}_{i,2}[\psi_{H}]\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini}).

In particular, this estimate is independent of Δ1\Delta_{1}.

By the Sobolev embedding theorems given by Proposition 7, we have thus closed our bootstrap assumption (A1) after choosing Δ1\Delta_{1} to be sufficiently large depending on the initial data norm 𝒪i​n​i\mathcal{O}_{ini}. We have therefore proved the desired estimates for the Ricci coefficients and their first three angular covariant derivatives. We summarize this in the following proposition.

Proposition 15.

Assume

ℛ<∞,𝒪~4,2<∞.\mathcal{R}<\infty,\quad\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{4,2}<\infty.

Then there exists ϵ0=ϵ0​(𝒪i​n​i,ℛ,𝒪~4,2)\epsilon_{0}=\epsilon_{0}(\mathcal{O}_{ini},\mathcal{R},\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{4,2}) such that whenever ϵ≤ϵ0\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{0},

∑i≤3𝒪i,2​[ψ,ψH¯,ψH]≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i).\sum_{i\leq 3}\mathcal{O}_{i,2}[\psi,\psi_{\underline{H}},\psi_{H}]\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini}).

7. Elliptic Estimates for Fourth Derivatives of the Ricci Coefficients

We now estimate the 4th derivative of the Ricci coefficients. We introduce the following bootstrap assumption:

𝒪~4,2≤Δ2,\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{4,2}\leq\Delta_{2}, (A2)

where Δ2\Delta_{2} is a constant to be chosen later.

The estimates for the 4th derivative of the Ricci coefficients cannot be achieved only by the transport equations since there would be a loss in derivatives. We can however use the transport equation - Hodge system type estimates as in [15, 5, 16]. We will first derive estimates for some chosen combination of ∇4(ψ,ψH,ψH¯)+∇3(β,K,σˇ,β¯)\nabla^{4}(\psi,\psi_{H},\psi_{\underline{H}})+{\nabla^{3}}(\beta,K,\check{\sigma},\underline{\beta}) by using transport equations. We will then show that the estimates for all the 4th derivatives of the Ricci coefficients can be proved via elliptic estimates.

In order to apply the elliptic estimates in Section 5.5, we need to first control the Gauss curvature and its first and second derivatives in L2​(S)L^{2}(S).

Proposition 16.

Assume

ℛ<∞.\mathcal{R}<\infty.

Then there exists ϵ0=ϵ0​(Δ2,ℛ)\epsilon_{0}=\epsilon_{0}(\Delta_{2},\mathcal{R}) such that whenever ϵ≤ϵ0\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{0},

∑i≤2‖∇iK‖Lu∞​Lu¯∞​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i).\sum_{i\leq 2}||\nabla^{i}K||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini}{)}.
Proof.

KK obeys the following Bianchi equation:

∇4K=∇β+ψH​K+∑i1+i2+i3≤1ψi1​∇i2ψ​∇i3ψH.\nabla_{4}K=\nabla\beta+\psi_{H}K+\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}\leq 1}\psi^{i_{1}}\nabla^{i_{2}}\psi\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}.

Commuting with angular derivatives, we have, for i≤2i\leq 2,

∇4∇i​K=∑i1+i2+i3≤2∇i1ψi2​∇i3+1β+∑i1+i2+i3+i4≤2∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψH​∇i4K+∑i1+i2+i3+i4≤3∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψ​∇i4ψH.\begin{split}&\nabla_{4}\nabla^{i}K\\ =&\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}\leq 2}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}+1}\beta+\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}\leq 2}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}\nabla^{i_{4}}K+\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}\leq 3}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{H}.\end{split}

By Proposition 5, in order to control ∇iK\nabla^{i}K in Lu∞​Lu¯∞​L2​(S)L^{\infty}_{u}L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S), we need to bound the right hand side in Lu∞​Lu¯1​L2​(S)L^{\infty}_{u}L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S). We first control the term containing β\beta:

‖∑i1+i2+i3≤2∇i1ψi2​∇i3+1β‖Lu∞​Lu¯1​L2​(S)≤C⁡(∑i1≤1,i2≤2‖∇i1ψ‖Lu∞​Lu¯∞​L∞​(S)i2)||f​(u¯)−1||Lu¯2​(∑i3≤2‖f⁡(u¯)​∇i2+1β‖Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S))≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​ϵ​ℛ,\begin{split}&||\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}\leq 2}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}+1}\beta||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\\ \leq&C(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 1,i_{2}\leq 2}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)}^{i_{2}})||f(\underline{u})^{-1}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}}(\sum_{i_{3}\leq 2}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{2}+1}\beta||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ \leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})\epsilon\mathcal{R},\end{split}

where we have used the estimates for ψ\psi given by Proposition 15. The term containing KK can be controlled by

‖∑i1+i2+i3+i4≤2∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψH​∇i4K‖Lu∞​Lu¯1​L2​(S)≤C⁡(∑i1≤1,i2≤2‖∇i1ψ‖Lu∞​Lu¯∞​L∞​(S)i2)​∫0u¯(∑i3+i4≤2‖∇i3ψH​∇i4K‖Lu∞​L2​(Su,u¯′))​d​u¯′≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​∫0u¯(∑i1+i2≤2‖∇i1ψH​∇i2K‖Lu∞​L2​(Su,u¯′))​d​u¯′≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​∫0u¯(∑i1≤2‖∇i1ψH‖Lu∞​L2​(Su,u¯′))​(∑i2≤2‖∇i2K‖Lu∞​L2​(Su,u¯′))​d​u¯′.\begin{split}&||\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}\leq 2}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}\nabla^{i_{4}}K||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\\ \leq&C(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 1,i_{2}\leq 2}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||^{i_{2}}_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}(S)})\int_{0}^{\underline{u}}(\sum_{i_{3}+i_{4}\leq 2}||\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}\nabla^{i_{4}}K||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}^{\prime}})})d\underline{u}^{\prime}\\ \leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})\int_{0}^{\underline{u}}(\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}\leq 2}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi_{H}\nabla^{i_{2}}K||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}^{\prime}})})d\underline{u}^{\prime}\\ \leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})\int_{0}^{\underline{u}}(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 2}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}^{\prime}})})(\sum_{i_{2}\leq 2}||\nabla^{i_{2}}K||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}^{\prime}})})d\underline{u}^{\prime}.\end{split}

The remaining term has been bounded in the previous section. By (42) and Proposition 15,

‖∑i1+i2+i3≤2ψi1​∇i2ψ​∇i3ψH‖Lu∞​Lu¯1​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​ϵ.||\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}\leq 2}\psi^{i_{1}}\nabla^{i_{2}}\psi\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})\epsilon.

Therefore, by Proposition 5,

∑i≤2‖∇iK‖Lu∞​L2​(Su,u¯)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​(1+ϵ+ϵ​ℛ+∫0u¯(∑i1≤2‖∇i1ψH‖Lu∞​L2​(Su,u¯′))​(∑i2≤2‖∇i2K‖Lu∞​L2​(Su,u¯′))​d​u¯′).\begin{split}&\sum_{i\leq 2}||\nabla^{i}K||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}})}\\ \leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})(1+\epsilon+\epsilon\mathcal{R}+\int_{0}^{\underline{u}}(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 2}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}^{\prime}})})(\sum_{i_{2}\leq 2}||\nabla^{i_{2}}K||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}^{\prime}})})d\underline{u}^{\prime}).\end{split}

Gronwall’s inequality implies

∑i≤2||∇iK||Lu∞​L2​(Su,u¯)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​exp⁡(∑i≤2‖∇iψH‖Lu¯1​Lu∞​L2​(S))≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)\begin{split}\sum_{i\leq 2}||\nabla^{i}K||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}})}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})\exp(\sum_{i\leq 2}||\nabla^{i}\psi_{H}||_{L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S)})\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})\end{split}

since by Proposition 15, ∑i≤1‖∇iψH‖Lu¯1​Lu∞​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)\displaystyle\sum_{i\leq 1}||\nabla^{i}\psi_{H}||_{L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini}) for ϵ\epsilon sufficiently small. ∎

It is easy to see that since σˇ\check{\sigma} satisfies a similar schematic Bianchi equation as KK, we also have the following estimates for σˇ\check{\sigma} and its derivative:

Proposition 17.

Assume

ℛ<∞.\mathcal{R}<\infty.

Then there exists ϵ0=ϵ0​(Δ2,ℛ)\epsilon_{0}=\epsilon_{0}(\Delta_{2},\mathcal{R}) such that whenever ϵ≤ϵ0\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{0},

∑i≤2‖∇iσˇ‖Lu∞​Lu¯∞​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i).\sum_{i\leq 2}||\nabla^{i}\check{\sigma}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini}).

Using Proposition 16, we now control the fourth derivatives of the Ricci coefficients. We first bound ∇4tr​χ\nabla^{4}\mbox{tr}\chi using the transport equation.

Proposition 18.

There exists ϵ0=ϵ0​(𝒪i​n​i,Δ2)\epsilon_{0}=\epsilon_{0}(\mathcal{O}_{ini},\Delta_{2}) such that whenever ϵ≤ϵ0\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{0},

‖f⁡(u¯)​∇4tr​χ‖Lu¯2​Lu∞​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i).||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{4}\mbox{tr}\chi||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini}).
Proof.

Consider the following equation:

∇4tr​χ=ψH​ψH,\nabla_{4}\mbox{tr}\chi=\psi_{H}\psi_{H},

After commuting with angular derivatives, we have

∇4∇4​tr​χ=∑i1+i2+i3+i4=4∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψH​∇i4ψH.\nabla_{4}\nabla^{4}\mbox{tr}\chi=\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}=4}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{H}.

By Proposition 5, in order to control ∇4tr​χ\nabla^{4}\mbox{tr}\chi in L2​(Su,u¯)L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}}) , we need to bound the right hand side in Lu¯1​L2​(S)L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S). Using the fact that f⁡(u¯)f(\underline{u}) is decreasing, this can be achieved using Sobolev embedding (Proposition 7) by

∑i1+i2+i3+i4≤4∫0u¯‖∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψH​∇i4ψH‖L2​(Su,u¯′)​d​u¯′≤C​f​(u¯)−2​(∑i1≤3∑i2≤4‖∇i1ψ‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S)i2)​(∑i3≤2‖f⁡(u¯)​∇i3ψH‖Lu¯2​L2​(S))​(∑i4≤4‖f⁡(u¯)​∇i4ψH‖Lu¯2​L2​(S))≤C​f​(u¯)−2​Δ2.\begin{split}&{\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}\leq 4}\int_{0}^{\underline{u}}}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}^{\prime}})}{d\underline{u}^{\prime}}\\ \leq&Cf(\underline{u})^{-2}(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 3}\sum_{i_{2}\leq 4}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||^{i_{2}}_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})(\sum_{i_{3}\leq 2}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})(\sum_{i_{4}\leq 4}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ \leq&Cf(\underline{u})^{-2}\Delta_{2}.\end{split}

By Proposition 5, we have

‖∇4tr​χ‖L2​(Su,u¯)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)+C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​f​(u¯)−2​Δ2.||\nabla^{4}\mbox{tr}\chi||_{L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}})}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})+C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})f(\underline{u})^{-2}\Delta_{2}. (47)

Multiplying (47) by f⁡(u¯)f(\underline{u}) and taking first the L∞L^{\infty} norm in uu and then the L2L^{2} norm in u¯\underline{u}, we have

‖f⁡(u¯)​∇4tr​χ‖Lu¯2​Lu∞​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)+C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​‖f​(u¯)−1‖Lu¯2​Δ2≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)+C​ϵ​Δ2,\begin{split}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{4}\mbox{tr}\chi||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}(S)}\leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})+C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})||f(\underline{u})^{-1}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}}\Delta_{2}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})+C\epsilon\Delta_{2},\end{split}

where we have used

‖f​(u¯)−1‖Lu¯2≤C​ϵ.||f(\underline{u})^{-1}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}}\leq C\epsilon.

Thus, the conclusion follows by choosing ϵ\epsilon to be sufficiently small depending on Δ2\Delta_{2}. ∎

Once we have the estimates for ∇4tr​χ\nabla^{4}\mbox{tr}\chi, we can control ∇4χ^\nabla^{4}\hat{\chi} using elliptic estimates:

Proposition 19.

Assume

ℛ<∞.\mathcal{R}<\infty.

Then there exists ϵ0=ϵ0​(𝒪i​n​i,Δ2,ℛ)\epsilon_{0}=\epsilon_{0}(\mathcal{O}_{ini},\Delta_{2},\mathcal{R}) such that whenever ϵ≤ϵ0\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{0},

‖f⁡(u¯)​∇4χ^‖Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)+C​ℛ.||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{4}\hat{\chi}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})+C\mathcal{R}.
Proof.

We now use the Codazzi equation

div χ^=12∇trχ−β+ψψH\mbox{div }\hat{\chi}=\frac{1}{2}\nabla\mbox{tr}\chi-\beta+\psi\psi_{H}

and apply elliptic estimates from Proposition 11 to get

‖∇4χ^‖L2​(S)≤C⁡(∑i≤4‖∇itr​χ‖L2​(S)+∑i≤3‖∇iβ‖L2​(S)+∑i1+i2≤3‖∇i1ψ​∇i2ψH‖L2​(S)+∑i≤3‖∇iχ^‖L2​(S)).\begin{split}&||\nabla^{4}\hat{\chi}||_{L^{2}(S)}\\ \leq&C(\sum_{i\leq 4}||\nabla^{i}\mbox{tr}\chi||_{L^{2}(S)}+\sum_{i\leq 3}||\nabla^{i}\beta||_{L^{2}(S)}+\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi\nabla^{i_{2}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{2}(S)}+\sum_{i\leq 3}||\nabla^{i}\hat{\chi}||_{L^{2}(S)}).\end{split} (48)

Notice that we can apply elliptic estimates using Proposition 11 since we have the estimates for the Gauss curvature from Proposition 16. Multiply (48) by f⁡(u¯)f(\underline{u}) and take the Lu∞​Lu¯2L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}} norm to get

‖f⁡(u¯)​∇4χ^‖Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S)≤C(∑i≤4||f(u¯)∇itrχ||Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S)+∑i≤3||f(u¯)∇iβ||Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S)+∑i1+i2≤3||f(u¯)∇i1ψ∇i2ψH||Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S)+∑i≤3||f(u¯)∇iχ^||Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S))≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)+C​ℛ+C​∑i1+i2≤3‖f⁡(u¯)​∇i1ψ​∇i2ψH‖Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S).\begin{split}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{4}\hat{\chi}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\leq&C(\sum_{i\leq 4}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i}\mbox{tr}\chi||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}({S})}+\sum_{i\leq 3}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i}\beta||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\\ &\quad+\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}\leq 3}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi\nabla^{i_{2}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}+\sum_{i\leq 3}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i}\hat{\chi}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ \leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})+C\mathcal{R}+C\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}\leq 3}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi\nabla^{i_{2}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}.\end{split}

By Proposition 15 and Sobolev embedding theorem in Proposition 7, we have

∑i1+i2≤3‖f⁡(u¯)​∇i1ψ​∇i2ψH‖Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(∑i1≤3‖∇i1ψ‖Lu∞​Lu¯∞​L2​(S))​(∑i2≤3‖f⁡(u¯)​∇i2ψH‖Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S))≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i).\begin{split}&\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}\leq 3}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi\nabla^{i_{2}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\\ \leq&C(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})(\sum_{i_{2}\leq 3}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{2}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini}).\end{split}

Therefore,

‖f⁡(u¯)​∇4χ^‖Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)+C​ℛ.||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{4}\hat{\chi}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})+C\mathcal{R}.

∎

The 𝒪~4,2\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{4,2} estimates for ∇4tr​χ¯\nabla^{4}\mbox{tr}\underline{\chi} and ∇4χ¯^\nabla^{4}\hat{\underline{\chi}} follow identically as that for ∇4tr​χ\nabla^{4}\mbox{tr}\chi and ∇4χ^\nabla^{4}\hat{\chi}:

Proposition 20.

Assume

ℛ<∞.\mathcal{R}<\infty.

Then there exists ϵ0=ϵ0​(𝒪i​n​i,Δ2,ℛ)\epsilon_{0}=\epsilon_{0}(\mathcal{O}_{ini},\Delta_{2},\mathcal{R}) such that whenever ϵ≤ϵ0\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{0},

‖f⁡(u)​∇4tr​χ¯‖Lu¯∞​Lu2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i),||f(u)\nabla^{4}\mbox{tr}\underline{\chi}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}_{u}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini}),

and

‖f⁡(u)​∇4χ¯^‖Lu¯∞​Lu2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)+C​ℛ.||f(u)\nabla^{4}\hat{\underline{\chi}}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}_{u}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})+C\mathcal{R}.

We then prove estimates for ∇4η\nabla^{4}\eta. To do so, we first prove estimates for third derivatives of μ=−div ​η+K\mu=-\mbox{div }\eta+K and recover the control for ∇4η\nabla^{4}\eta via elliptic estimates.

Proposition 21.

Assume

ℛ<∞.\mathcal{R}<\infty.

Then there exists ϵ0=ϵ0​(𝒪i​n​i,Δ2,ℛ)\epsilon_{0}=\epsilon_{0}(\mathcal{O}_{ini},\Delta_{2},\mathcal{R}) such that whenever ϵ≤ϵ0\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{0},

‖f⁡(u)​∇4η‖Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​(ϵ12+ℛ),||f(u)\nabla^{4}\eta||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})(\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}+\mathcal{R}),

and

‖f⁡(u¯)​∇4η‖Lu¯∞​Lu2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​(ϵ12+ℛ).||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{4}\eta||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}_{u}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})(\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}+\mathcal{R}).
Proof.

Recall that

μ=−div ​η+K.\mu=-\mbox{div }\eta+K.

Then μ\mu satisfies the following equation2626 26 It is important to note that the potentially harmful term ψH¯​ψH​ψH\psi_{\underline{H}}\psi_{H}\psi_{H} is absent in this equation. This required structure is the reason that we perform this renormalization instead of using μ=−div ​η−ρ+12​χ^⋅χ¯^\mu=-\mbox{div }\eta-\rho+\frac{1}{2}\hat{\chi}\cdot\hat{\underline{\chi}} as in [19, 18].:

∇4μ=ψH​(K,σˇ)+∑i1+i2+i3=1ψi1​∇i2ψ​∇i3ψH.\nabla_{4}\mu=\psi_{H}(K,\check{\sigma})+\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}=1}\psi^{i_{1}}\nabla^{i_{2}}\psi\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}.

After commuting with angular derivatives, we get

∇4∇3​μ=∑i1+i2+i3+i4=3∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψH​∇i4(K,σˇ)+∑i1+i2+i3+i4=4∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψ​∇i4ψH.\begin{split}\nabla_{4}\nabla^{3}\mu=&\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}=3}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}\nabla^{i_{4}}(K,\check{\sigma})+\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}=4}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{H}.\end{split}

We now control each of the terms on the right hand side in Lu¯1​L2​(S)L^{1}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S). The first term, which contains curvature components, can be estimated by

∑i1+i2+i3+i4=3∫0u¯‖∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψH​∇i4(K,σˇ)‖L2​(Su,u¯′)​d​u¯′≤C​f​(u)−1​f​(u¯)−1​(∑i1≤3∑i2≤3‖∇i1ψ‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S)i2)​(∑i3≤3‖f⁡(u¯)​∇i3ψH‖Lu¯2​L2​(S))×(∑i4≤3‖f⁡(u)​∇i4(K,σˇ)‖Lu¯2​L2​(S))≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​f​(u)−1​f​(u¯)−1​ℛ,\begin{split}&{\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}=3}\int_{0}^{\underline{u}}}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}\nabla^{i_{4}}(K,\check{\sigma})||_{L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}^{\prime}})}{d\underline{u}^{\prime}}\\ \leq&Cf(u)^{-1}f(\underline{u})^{-1}(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 3}\sum_{i_{2}\leq 3}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||^{i_{2}}_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})(\sum_{i_{3}\leq 3}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ &\quad\quad\times(\sum_{i_{4}\leq 3}||f(u)\nabla^{i_{4}}(K,\check{\sigma})||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ \leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})f(u)^{-1}f(\underline{u})^{-1}\mathcal{R},\end{split}

using the bounds obtained in Proposition 15. The second term can be controlled using Sobolev embedding in Proposition 7 by

∑i1+i2+i3+i4=4∫0u¯‖∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψ​∇i4ψH‖L2​(Su,u¯′)​d​u¯′≤C​f​(u)−1​f​(u¯)−1​(∑i1≤4∑i2≤5‖∇i1ψ‖Lu¯∞​L2​(S)i2)​(∑i3≤4‖f⁡(u¯)​∇i3ψH‖Lu¯2​L2​(S))​(∑i4≤4‖f⁡(u)​∇i4ψ‖Lu¯2​L2​(S))≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​f​(u)−1​f​(u¯)−1​(1+Δ2)2\begin{split}&{\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}=4}\int_{0}^{\underline{u}}}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}^{\prime}})}{d\underline{u}^{\prime}}\\ \leq&Cf(u)^{-1}f(\underline{u})^{-1}(\sum_{i_{1}\leq 4}\sum_{i_{2}\leq 5}||\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi||^{i_{2}}_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})(\sum_{i_{3}\leq 4}||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})(\sum_{i_{4}\leq 4}||f(u)\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ \leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})f(u)^{-1}f(\underline{u})^{-1}(1+\Delta_{2})^{2}\end{split}

using the estimates in Proposition 15. Therefore, by Proposition 5, we have

‖∇3μ‖L2​(Su,u¯)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​(1+f​(u)−1​f​(u¯)−1​(ℛ+(1+Δ2)2)).\begin{split}||\nabla^{3}\mu||_{L^{2}(S_{u,\underline{u}})}\leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})(1+f(u)^{-1}f(\underline{u})^{-1}(\mathcal{R}+(1+\Delta_{2})^{2})).\end{split} (49)

Recall that the Lu¯2L^{2}_{\underline{u}} norm of f​(u¯)−1f(\underline{u})^{-1} is bounded by ϵ\epsilon. Thus, multiplying (49) by f⁡(u)f(u) and taking the L2L^{2} norm in u¯\underline{u}, we get

‖f⁡(u)​∇3μ‖Lu¯2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​(ϵ12+ϵ⁡(ℛ+(1+Δ2)2))≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​ϵ12,\begin{split}||f(u)\nabla^{3}\mu||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})(\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}+\epsilon(\mathcal{R}+(1+\Delta_{2})^{2}))\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}},\end{split}

for ϵ\epsilon sufficiently small. Similarly, multiplying (49) by f⁡(u¯)f(\underline{u}) and taking the L2L^{2} norm in uu, we get

‖f⁡(u¯)​∇3μ‖Lu2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​ϵ12.||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{3}\mu||_{L^{2}_{u}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}.

We can obtain bounds for ∇4η\nabla^{4}\eta from the control of ∇3μ\nabla^{3}\mu using elliptic estimates as follows. By the div-curl systems

div ​η=−μ+K,curl ​η=σˇ,\mbox{div }\eta=-\mu+K,\quad\mbox{curl }\eta=\check{\sigma},

and the elliptic estimates given by Propositions 10 and 16, we have

‖∇4η‖L2​(S)≤C⁡(∑i≤3‖∇iμ‖L2​(S)+∑i≤3‖∇i(K,σˇ)‖L2​(S)+∑i≤3‖∇iη‖L2​(S)).||\nabla^{4}\eta||_{L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\sum_{i\leq 3}||\nabla^{i}\mu||_{L^{2}(S)}+\sum_{i\leq 3}||\nabla^{i}(K,\check{\sigma})||_{L^{2}(S)}+\sum_{i\leq 3}||\nabla^{i}\eta||_{L^{2}(S)}).

Therefore,

‖f⁡(u)​∇4η‖Lu¯2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(∑i≤3‖f⁡(u)​∇iμ‖Lu¯2​L2​(S)+∑i≤3‖f⁡(u)​∇i(K,σˇ)‖Lu¯2​L2​(S)+∑i≤3‖f⁡(u)​∇iη‖Lu¯2​L2​(S))≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​(ϵ12+ℛ).\begin{split}&||f(u)\nabla^{4}\eta||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\\ \leq&C(\sum_{i\leq 3}||f(u)\nabla^{i}\mu||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}+\sum_{i\leq 3}||f(u)\nabla^{i}(K,\check{\sigma})||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}+\sum_{i\leq 3}||f(u)\nabla^{i}\eta||_{L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)})\\ \leq&C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})(\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}+\mathcal{R}).\end{split}

Similarly,

‖f⁡(u¯)​∇4η‖Lu2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​(ϵ12+ℛ).||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{4}\eta||_{L^{2}_{u}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})(\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}+\mathcal{R}).

∎

A similar proof shows that the conclusion of Proposition 21 holds also for ∇3η¯\nabla^{3}\underline{\eta}:

Proposition 22.

Assume

ℛ<∞.\mathcal{R}<\infty.

Then there exists ϵ0=ϵ0​(𝒪i​n​i,Δ2,ℛ)\epsilon_{0}=\epsilon_{0}(\mathcal{O}_{ini},\Delta_{2},\mathcal{R}) such that whenever ϵ≤ϵ0\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{0},

‖f⁡(u)​∇4η¯‖Lu∞​Lu¯2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​(ϵ12+ℛ),||f(u)\nabla^{4}\underline{\eta}||_{L^{\infty}_{u}L^{2}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})(\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}+\mathcal{R}),

and

‖f⁡(u¯)​∇4η¯‖Lu¯∞​Lu2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​(ϵ12+ℛ).||f(\underline{u})\nabla^{4}\underline{\eta}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}_{u}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})(\epsilon^{\frac{1}{2}}+\mathcal{R}).

We now move to the estimates for ∇4ω¯\nabla^{4}\underline{\omega}:

Proposition 23.

Assume

ℛ<∞.\mathcal{R}<\infty.

Then there exists ϵ0=ϵ0​(𝒪i​n​i,Δ2,ℛ)\epsilon_{0}=\epsilon_{0}(\mathcal{O}_{ini},\Delta_{2},\mathcal{R}) such that whenever ϵ≤ϵ0\epsilon\leq\epsilon_{0},

‖f⁡(u)​∇4ω¯‖Lu¯∞​Lu2​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i)​(1+ℛ).||f(u)\nabla^{4}\underline{\omega}||_{L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}_{u}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini})(1+\mathcal{R}).
Proof.

Let ω¯†\underline{\omega}^{\dagger} be defined as the solution to

∇4ω¯†=12​σˇ\nabla_{4}\underline{\omega}^{\dagger}=\frac{1}{2}\check{\sigma}

with zero data on H¯0\underline{H}_{0} and

κ¯:=−∇ω¯+∗∇ω¯†−12β¯.\underline{\kappa}:=-\nabla\underline{\omega}+^{*}\nabla\underline{\omega}^{\dagger}-\frac{1}{2}\underline{\beta}.

By the definition of ω¯†\underline{\omega}^{\dagger}, it is easy to see that using Proposition 5,

∑i≤3‖∇iω¯†‖Lu2​Lu¯∞​L2​(S)≤C​ϵ​ℛ≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i).\sum_{i\leq 3}||\nabla^{i}\underline{\omega}^{\dagger}||_{L^{2}_{u}L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\leq C\epsilon\mathcal{R}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini}).

In other words, ∇iω¯†{\nabla^{i}}\underline{\omega}^{\dagger} satisfies much better estimates2727 27 We recall that for ψH¯\psi_{\underline{H}} we only have the degenerate estimate ∑i≤3‖f⁡(u)​∇iψH¯‖Lu2​Lu¯∞​L2​(S)≤C⁡(𝒪i​n​i).\sum_{i\leq 3}||f(u)\nabla^{i}\psi_{\underline{H}}||_{L^{2}_{u}L^{\infty}_{\underline{u}}L^{2}(S)}\leq C(\mathcal{O}_{ini}). than ∇iψH¯{\nabla^{i}}\psi_{\underline{H}} for i≤3i\leq 3. With this in mind, in the proof of this proposition, we will also use ψH¯\psi_{\underline{H}} to denote ω¯†\underline{\omega}^{\dagger} (in addition to tr​χ¯\mbox{tr}\underline{\chi}, χ¯^\hat{\underline{\chi}} and ω¯\underline{\omega}).

With this convention, κ¯\underline{\kappa} then obeys the following schematic equation:

∇4κ¯=ψ⁡(K,σˇ)+∑i1+i2+i3=1ψi1​∇i2ψ​∇i3ψ+∑i1+i2+i3=1ψi1​∇i2ψH​∇i3ψH¯.\nabla_{4}\underline{\kappa}=\psi(K,\check{\sigma})+\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}=1}\psi^{i_{1}}\nabla^{i_{2}}\psi\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi+\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}=1}\psi^{i_{1}}\nabla^{i_{2}}\psi_{H}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{\underline{H}}.

After commuting with angular derivatives, we get

∇4∇3​κ¯=∑i1+i2+i3+i4=3∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψ​∇i4(K,σˇ)+∑i1+i2+i3+i4=4∇i1ψi2​∇i3ψ​∇i4ψ+∑i1+i2+i3+i4=4∇i1ψi2∇i3ψH∇i4ψH¯.\begin{split}\nabla_{4}\nabla^{3}\underline{\kappa}=&\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}=3}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi\nabla^{i_{4}}(K,\check{\sigma})+\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}=4}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi\\ &+\sum_{i_{1}+i_{2}+i_{3}+i_{4}=4}\nabla^{i_{1}}\psi^{i_{2}}\nabla^{i_{3}}\psi_{H}\nabla^{i_{4}}\psi_{\underline{H}}.\\ \end{split}

Therefore,

Proposition 35.

Suppose the assumptions of Theorem 4 hold. Then, the Christoffel symbols in the (u,u¯,θ1,θ2)(u,\underline{u},\theta^{1},\theta^{2}) coordinate system are not in L2L^{2} in a neighborhood of any point on Hu∗H_{u_{*}} or H¯u¯∗\underline{H}_{\underline{u}_{*}}.
